findings.title: Hardcoded credential-like value
findings.description: A variable or property whose name suggests a secret is assigned a string literal. Secrets in source code can leak through version control.
findings.next_step: Confirm whether this is a real secret or a placeholder; if real, rotate it and load it from configuration or a secret store instead.
limitations: The matched value is redacted; the rule cannot tell real secrets from test placeholders.
Secrets assembled at runtime or stored in non-source files are not detected.

findings.title: SQL query built with string interpolation
findings.description: A string that looks like a SQL statement is built from a template literal or concatenation with non-constant values. If any interpolated value is user-controlled, this may allow SQL injection.
findings.evidence: const sql = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '${email}'`;
findings.next_step: Check whether the interpolated values can come from request input (trace the enclosing function's callers) and whether the query is executed with parameter binding instead.
limitations: The rule does not track where interpolated values originate.
Sanitization performed before this line is not detected.
